# Surp v1.2.0

Surp `v1.2.0` documents the current repository architecture and captures the
active defect inventory across the Rust workspace, Python binding layer, CLI,
FFI surface, and MCP server.

## Architecture

- `surp-core` remains the shared engine crate for v1 `Value` / `Encoder` /
  `Decoder` behavior and the RFC-001 implementation.
- `surp-derive` provides the proc-macros for `#[derive(Surp)]` and
  `#[derive(SurpSchema)]`.
- `surp-io` provides Tokio streaming and mmap-oriented helpers.
- `surp-compression` remains a pluggable compressor trait crate, but is still
  orphaned and unused by the rest of the workspace.
- `surp-simd` provides NEON-oriented scan helpers, but is still orphaned and
  unused by the rest of the workspace.
- `surp-ffi` exposes the C ABI with JSON-in / JSON-out entry points.
- `surp-cli` ships the binary command-line interface.
- `surp-python` combines the PyO3 native extension with the pure-Python
  `surp.model` ORM layer.
- `surp-mcp` is a separate stdio JSON-RPC server and is not a workspace member;
  it currently has zero CI coverage.
- `surp_docs` is the standalone site, while `bench`, `fuzz`, and `examples`
  are supporting tooling.

The release also reflects the two parallel format pipelines that currently live
side by side:

- v1: `Value` / `Encoder` / `Decoder`, block-framed with XXH64 per block plus a
  trailer checksum.
- RFC-001: CTN text -> `ast::Document` -> CBF binary, CRC64 trailer, and CQL
  selector queries.

The Python data flow remains dict/list -> PyO3 `py_to_value` -> `Value` ->
`Encoder` -> bytes -> `PyBytes`, with the reverse path for decode. The GIL is
held for the whole call path, and there is no `allow_threads` usage anywhere in
that flow.

## Defects

### Critical

- C1: `surp-core/src/rfc001/ctn.rs:465` allocates `<binary: N bytes>` directly
  from untrusted text with `vec![0u8; N]` and no cap.
- C2: `surp-python/src/lib.rs:120-144` mixes `is_instance_of` with
  `cast_exact`, so dict/list/tuple subclasses can fail with raw PyO3 exceptions
  instead of `SurpTypeError`.
- C3: `surp-python/src/lib.rs:91-182` recurses with no depth counter, so deep
  Python structures can overflow the native stack instead of raising
  `RecursionError`.
- C4: `surp-python/Cargo.toml:18-20` and `surp-core/src/encoder.rs:343-365`
  leave zstd/lz4/snappy wiring incomplete for Python wheels, so compression
  requests can silently fall back to uncompressed output.

### High

- H1: `surp-core/src/rfc001/cbf.rs:893,947,959,1014,1067,1459` preallocate
  CBF containers from untrusted counts before validating the payload.
- H2: `surp-core/src/decoder.rs:558-576,599-614` uses self-recursion to skip
  non-Data blocks, which can overflow the stack on many consecutive blocks.
- H3: `surp-core/src/rfc001/ctn.rs` has no nesting-depth limit in the parser.
- H4: `surp-io/src/lib.rs:98-105` allocates `vec![0u8; remaining]` from
  stream-controlled block lengths with no Limits cap.
- H5: `surp-mcp/src/registry.rs:375` infers read-only vs destructive hints by
  name substring, which is wrong for several file-writing tools.
- H6: `surp-mcp/src/protocol.rs:49-56,71` reads inbound JSON-RPC without a line
  cap and parses JSON without a recursion limit.
- H7: `surp-mcp/src/ops.rs:706-737` bypasses input-size checks for inline value
  tool arguments.
- H8: `surp-derive/src/lib.rs:88-131` still needs better compile-time hygiene
  for malformed and duplicate `#[surp(id = ...)]` attributes.
- H9: `surp-simd/src/lib.rs:140-151` performs a NEON pre-scan but still runs the
  full scalar decode path in release builds.
- H11: `surp-ffi/src/lib.rs:23-129` lacks `catch_unwind` around `extern "C"`
  entry points.

### Medium / Low

- Owned decode paths do not fully track allocations for container-heavy payloads
  in `surp-core`.
- Text pretty-printing does not escape keys containing `\/\` characters
  correctly.
- The encoder does not enforce `max_string_length` at encode time, even though
  the decoder enforces it.
- `BumpDecoder`'s arena is effectively dead code during actual decode.
- RFC-001 CRC64 remains a naive bit-loop implementation.
- CBF sequence and map encode paths double-buffer their payloads.
- Infallible integer trait paths can still panic for `u128` / `i128`.
- `block.rs` contains a duplicate block-framing implementation without a size
  guard.
- Python error classification relies on string matching and collapses many Rust
  error variants into a few Python exceptions.
- Python RFC-001 query helpers are still incomplete and `allow_threads` is not
  used anywhere in the binding layer.
- `surp-compression` and `surp-core` currently maintain separate compression
  implementations.

## Validation

Validated locally with:

```sh
cargo test -p surp-derive --test derive_types --test trybuild
cargo test -p surp-cli --test cli_integration --test cli_rfc001
```

## Notes

- Release tag: `v1.2.0`
- Release title: `Surp v1.2.0`
- This release is a documentation and architecture snapshot; it does not change
  wire compatibility.
- RFC-001 remains separate from the v1 `.surp` format.
- The MCP server remains outside the Rust workspace and has no CI coverage.
